key_insight: 4-bit AdamW fails mainly because quantization should be designed in preconditioner space, not just state space, since small state errors can cause large next-step preconditioner distortions.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides two practical 4-bit optimizer-state recipes—ZIP-SR and ZE-EDEN—that improve training stability and validation loss while preserving the memory savings needed for large-model training.
method: ZIP-SR: keep zero in the second-moment codebook and do stochastic rounding in preconditioner space.
ZE-EDEN: use a zero-excluding second-moment codebook with EDEN rescaling to reduce positive-floor distortion.
Use 4-bit NF4 for the first moment, with targeted stochastic rounding of the LM-head first moment during the final 10% of training.
evidence_signal: Across GPT- and Llama-style pretraining from 130M to 2.7B parameters, both methods reduced the validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW at every evaluated size, with up to 70% gap reduction, and also beat TorchAO in supervised fine-tuning.
watch_item: The methods depend on careful codebook design and targeted rounding schedules, so implementation details and training-phase tuning may affect reproducibility and generalization.
paper_title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
